etymology.historical_story: x 随拉丁字母体系成为现代马来语 Rumi 书写系统的一员，DBP 拼写指南将其字母名称列为 eks。后来在非正式数字交流中，同一字符又被用来简写 tak，于是一个字符同时承担了字母标记与聊天速记两种功能。[DBP：马来语拼写指南](https://eseminar.dbp.gov.my/dokumen/ejaan.pdf)

etymology.historical_story: Xiao represents the Chinese name 簫, simplified 箫, in pinyin spelling. Historically, the name referred to different wind instruments, so an ancient mention does not always identify today's vertical flute. The instrument became associated with scholarly refinement and intimate music making, including duets with the qin. See [Grinnell College's instrument collection](https://omeka-s.grinnell.edu/s/MusicalInstruments/item/1250).

etymology.historical_story: Xianyang represents the Mandarin place name Xiányáng, written 咸阳. A traditional explanation links the name to its position south of Jiuzong Mountain and north of the Wei River: both positions count as yang in Chinese geographical terminology. The explanation preserves a landscape-based naming tradition rather than any Malay morphological structure. [Source: China Tourism News](https://www.ctnews.com.cn/dongtai/content/2025-04/21/content_172934.html).

etymology.historical_story: Xavier began as a place-associated name rather than a Malay descriptive word. Its history connects with Javier in Navarre, whose older Basque name Etxeberri means 'new house'. Saint Francis Xavier helped give the name international recognition. This background explains its appearance in personal and institutional names, but does not establish a separate common-word meaning in Malay.
